prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (2017 manifesto)

Europe and Brexit
- Hold a referendum on the negotiated EU deal with the option to remain.
- Seek single market and customs union membership; guarantee rights of EU and UK citizens; protect Erasmus+, research funding, security cooperation, travel benefits, and regional interests (including Gibraltar and Northern Ireland).

Health and social care
- Immediate 1p rise on all Income Tax bands, ringfenced for the NHS and social care; plan a dedicated health and care tax and an independent budget watchdog.
- Integrate health and social care, cap social care costs, and support carers.
- End public sector pay cap; reinstate nurse bursaries; guarantee EU staff rights.
- Mental health parity with waiting-time standards, crisis care, talking therapies, perinatal support, and end out‑of‑area placements.

Education and skills
- Nearly £7bn extra for schools and colleges, protect per‑pupil funding, strengthen the Pupil Premium, fair funding formula.
- Tripled Early Years Pupil Premium; raise early-years staff qualifications.
- End 1% pay cap for teachers; guaranteed QTS; funded professional development.
- Oppose new selective schools; restore local role in school places; improve SEND support.
- Slimmed core curriculum with PSHE/SRE; protect arts; improve technical education, careers advice, and employer links.
- Reinstate maintenance grants; review higher education finance; protect universities’ international links.
- Double employers hiring apprentices; expand higher vocational routes; lifelong learning accounts; basic skills target by 2030.

Economy and work
- Eliminate day‑to‑day deficit by 2020; £100bn infrastructure plan (housing, schools, hospitals, rail/road, hyperfast fibre, renewables); create a Housing & Infrastructure Bank.
- Tax reforms: tackle avoidance, review business rates, consider land value tax; reverse recent cuts benefiting higher earners/large firms.
- Expand British Business Bank; startup allowance; scale-up mentoring.
- Boost R&D and green innovation; nationwide hyperfast broadband; support creative industries and digital skills.
- Promote a genuine living wage in the public sector; curb exploitative zero‑hours; strengthen employment rights and enforcement; enhance pay transparency and worker participation.

Environment, energy, and farming
- Five green laws covering transport, zero carbon, nature, buildings, and zero waste.
- Air Quality Plan: diesel scrappage; ban sale of new diesel cars/small vans by 2025; extend ultra‑low‑emission zones; expand charging.
- Target 60% electricity from renewables by 2030; support storage, smart grids, CCS; oppose fracking; conditional support for nuclear; remain in Euratom.
- Insulate 4m homes by 2022; restore zero‑carbon homes; expand community energy; boost market competition.
- £2bn flood‑prevention fund; statutory nature targets; protect rivers, coasts, and woodlands.
- Reform farm support toward public goods; fair supply chains; high import standards; sustainable fisheries plan.

Housing and communities
- Build 300,000 homes/year by 2022, including 500,000 affordable; garden cities; lift borrowing caps for councils/HAs; stronger planning obligations.
- Rent to Own; ban lettings fees; cap deposits; longer tenancies; tenant first refusal; tackle rogue landlords; end rough sleeping via Housing First.

Transport
- Invest in rail (electrification, HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2), stations, and freight to rail; government-run takeovers for failing franchises; ombudsman for passengers.
- Devolve bus powers; 16–21 Bus Discount Card; smart ticketing; cycling/walking investment.

Rights, justice, and immigration
- Keep the Human Rights Act/ECHR; digital bill of rights; independent press regulation.
- Extra £300m for community policing; body-worn cameras; replace PCCs; maintain EU justice tools.
- Presumption against short prison sentences; expand restorative justice; Women’s Justice Board.
- Decriminalise possession for personal use; regulated cannabis market.
- Efficient, fair immigration system; remove students from migration stats; STEM post‑study visas; Migration Impact Fund; more English language classes.
- Expand refugee resettlement (including unaccompanied children); end indefinite detention (28‑day limit).

International and defence
- Support UN, NATO; spend 0.7% GNI on aid and 2% GDP on defence; tighter arms export controls (suspend to Saudi Arabia).
- Maintain a reduced but minimum nuclear deterrent (three-boat posture); strengthen cyber capabilities.

Political and constitutional reform
- Votes at 16; proportional voting (STV) for local and Westminster elections; reform the Lords; cap donations; stronger lobbying rules; devolution on demand; constitutional convention; protect devolved settlements and Good Friday provisions.
